---
title: Receive webhooks
description: Register a webhook, check that each delivery came from your instance, and handle repeats, deliveries that arrive out of order, retries and failed deliveries.
---

A webhook lets a service react to changes without holding a connection open: you register a URL, and Marfa posts each event you chose to it. [Events](/build/events) explains when to use a webhook rather than the event stream.

You need your own Marfa instance, with the CLI signed in to it, as the [Quickstart](/quickstart) leaves you. Make the receiving service a key that holds `webhooks.manage` and reads the types it's told about:

```bash
marfa keys create --label "Note hook" --source note-hook \
  --permission webhooks.manage --type-permission core.note=read
```

**A webhook belongs to the key or app that registered it**: only that one can read, change or delete it. Marfa sends it nothing once the key is revoked or expires, and deletes it when the app's access is revoked. Each key or app can hold 100 webhooks.

## Register a webhook

[Create a webhook](/reference/api/webhooks/createWebhook) takes the `url` to post to and the `events` you want, each named from the Catalog's [Events](/catalog/events): there is no wildcard. `type_filter` limits item events and `metadata.changed` to one type and its subtypes, and leaves edge events as they are.

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa webhooks create --delivery-url https://example.com/marfa \
  --event item.created --event item.updated --type-filter core.note
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /webhooks
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "url": "https://example.com/marfa",
  "events": ["item.created", "item.updated"],
  "type_filter": "core.note"
}
```

Marfa answers with the webhook, its `secret` included:

```json title="Response" status="201"
{
  "id": "01a1f129-39f3-759b-84ea-b791ecb64764",
  "url": "https://example.com/marfa",
  "events": ["item.created", "item.updated"],
  "type_filter": "core.note",
  "secret": "dfaa1787b11d7e7223ac25bf0951c25b70f3985d5b737d8943eb03d2279d06a7",
  "active": true,
  "created_at": "2026-11-19T00:16:10.512Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-19T00:16:10.512Z"
}
```

Marfa shows the secret **only this once** (the CLI prints it alone on the first line); later reads show its last four characters. To choose your own, send `secret` with at least 32 characters.

The webhook receives only events written after you register it. A `url` that isn't public is refused unless [the instance allows it](#receive-deliveries-on-a-private-network).

## Check each delivery

A delivery is a `POST` whose body is the event as the stream sends it, plus `event_id`, the event's ID in the log; `delivery_id`, the same on every attempt; and `delivered_at`, when Marfa sent this attempt. The event type and the signature arrive as headers (shortened here):

```http title="Request"
POST /marfa
Content-Type: application/json
X-Marfa-Event-Type: item.updated
X-Marfa-Signature: t=1795047415,v1=02cf60cdfab91dc4c0b59be82d09af59ef11b124d2b3a31b5cb52c771df46f98

{
  "event_type": "item.updated",
  "item": {
    "id": "01a1f129-55c9-75e8-ac63-f21787875a7c",
    "type": "core.note",
    "state": "active",
    "version": 4,
    "properties": { "title": "Reading list", "body": "Start with the essays, then the letters." }
  },
  "metadata": { "item_id": "01a1f129-55c9-75e8-ac63-f21787875a7c", "tags": [], "extensions": {} },
  "event_id": "29",
  "delivery_id": "01a1f129-dfa6-703f-8e00-3a7400ff6497",
  "delivered_at": "2026-11-19T00:16:55.723Z"
}
```

Anyone can post to your URL, so check `X-Marfa-Signature` before you trust a delivery. It reads `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`, where `v1` is the HMAC-SHA-256, under your secret, of `t`, a period, and the raw body. Compute it over the bytes **exactly as they arrived**: parsing the JSON and serializing it again changes them.

The receiver needs Node.js 22.18 or later and only its built-in modules. `verify-signature.mts` refuses a delivery signed more than five minutes away from now, so a captured one can't be replayed, and compares the signatures in constant time. Marfa signs every attempt afresh, so a retry of an old event still passes:

```ts title="verify-signature.mts"
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

export function verifySignature(
  rawBody: Buffer,
  header: string | undefined,
  secret: string,
  toleranceSeconds = 300,
): boolean {
  if (header === undefined) return false;
  const fields = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const part of header.split(",")) {
    const at = part.indexOf("=");
    if (at > 0) fields.set(part.slice(0, at).trim(), part.slice(at + 1).trim());
  }
  const t = fields.get("t");
  const v1 = fields.get("v1");
  if (t === undefined || !/^\d+$/.test(t)) return false;
  if (v1 === undefined || !/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/i.test(v1)) return false;
  if (Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(t)) > toleranceSeconds) return false;

  const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${t}.`).update(rawBody).digest();
  const received = Buffer.from(v1, "hex");
  return received.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(received, expected);
}
```

`receiver.mts` answers before it does any work, skips a delivery it has handled, and answers `400` to a body it can't read:

```ts title="receiver.mts"
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { verifySignature } from "./verify-signature.mts";

const secret = process.env.MARFA_WEBHOOK_SECRET;
if (!secret) throw new Error("Set MARFA_WEBHOOK_SECRET to the webhook's secret.");
const handled = new Set<string>(); // keep this in your database

createServer((request, response) => {
  const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
  request.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => chunks.push(chunk));
  request.on("error", () => response.destroy());
  request.on("end", () => {
    try {
      const rawBody = Buffer.concat(chunks);
      const signature = request.headers["x-marfa-signature"];
      if (!verifySignature(rawBody, typeof signature === "string" ? signature : undefined, secret)) {
        response.writeHead(401).end();
        return;
      }

      const delivery = JSON.parse(rawBody.toString("utf8"));
      response.writeHead(204).end();
      if (handled.has(delivery.delivery_id)) return; // a repeat
      handled.add(delivery.delivery_id);

      console.log(delivery.event_type, delivery.event_id, delivery.item?.id);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(error);
      if (!response.headersSent) response.writeHead(400).end();
    }
  });
}).listen(3000);
```

```bash
MARFA_WEBHOOK_SECRET=<the secret> node receiver.mts
```

It holds the whole body before checking it, so **a receiver open to the internet should cap the body's size**, answering `413` above it.

## Answer, and recognize a repeat

Answer with a `2xx` status **within 10 seconds**, or the attempt counts as not answered, so do slow work afterward or in a queue. Marfa can deliver an event more than once, such as when your answer was lost, with the same `delivery_id` each time: record the IDs you've handled, as the receiver does.

## Expect deliveries out of order

Marfa sends one delivery at a time to each webhook, but a delivery that failed waits for its retry while newer ones go through.

`event_id` rises with every event. It's a string of decimal digits, so compare IDs as numbers: as text, `"99"` sorts after `"252"`. Keep the highest `event_id` you've applied for each item and ignore a delivery with a lower one, or treat a delivery as a prompt to [get the item](/reference/api/items/getItem) again.

## When a delivery fails

Marfa tries a delivery again when your receiver can't be reached, doesn't answer in time, or answers `5xx`, `408` or `429`. It makes eight attempts, waiting 1, 5, 25, 125, 625, 3,125 and 15,625 seconds between them. A `Retry-After` header asks it to wait longer, up to five minutes. Any other `4xx`, or a redirect, ends the delivery at once: Marfa never follows a redirect.

A delivery Marfa gives up on is `failed`. Because the receiver above answers `401` to a bad signature, a wrong secret fails the delivery at once instead of retrying it for hours. [List webhook deliveries](/reference/api/webhooks/listWebhookDeliveries) shows each delivery, newest first, with its `status` and your receiver's last answer:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa webhooks deliveries 01a1f129-39f3-759b-84ea-b791ecb64764 --json
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /webhooks/01a1f129-39f3-759b-84ea-b791ecb64764/deliveries
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
```

```json title="Response" status="200"
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "01a1f129-8222-708f-9ddc-1483d55cd7ee",
      "status": "failed",
      "webhook_id": "01a1f129-39f3-759b-84ea-b791ecb64764",
      "event_type": "item.updated",
      "status_code": 401,
      "attempt": 1,
      "succeeded": false,
      "error": "HTTP 401",
      "created_at": "2026-11-19T00:16:31.777Z"
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

A delivery's `status` is `pending`, `succeeded`, `failed` or `canceled`, and `attempt` counts attempts across every redelivery. Once you've fixed the fault, [Redeliver a webhook delivery](/reference/api/webhooks/redeliverWebhookDelivery) sends a `failed` delivery again with the same `delivery_id`, to the webhook's current URL and signed with its current secret. It answers `202` with the delivery as `pending`, and Marfa sends it shortly after, with eight attempts of its own:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa webhooks redeliver 01a1f129-39f3-759b-84ea-b791ecb64764 01a1f129-8222-708f-9ddc-1483d55cd7ee
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /webhooks/01a1f129-39f3-759b-84ea-b791ecb64764/deliveries/01a1f129-8222-708f-9ddc-1483d55cd7ee/redeliver
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
```

A refusal is `409 conflict`, with the reason in `details.reason`:

- **`webhook_inactive`:** the webhook is turned off.
- **`credential_unavailable`:** the key or app that registered it is no longer valid, or lacks `webhooks.manage`.
- **`delivery_not_failed`:** the delivery isn't `failed`.
- **`delivery_expired`:** the delivery is older than the instance keeps delivery records, 90 days by default (`audit_retention_days`).

## Change what a webhook sends

[Update a webhook](/reference/api/webhooks/updateWebhook) changes its `url`, `events`, `type_filter` or `active`. **A change cancels the pending deliveries it no longer allows**: narrowing `events` or `type_filter` cancels those no longer selected, and changing the `url` or turning the webhook off cancels them all. Deleting a webhook sends none of its pending deliveries.

## Receive deliveries on a private network

By default, Marfa refuses `400 validation_error` a `url` whose host, or the address its name leads to, isn't public, such as `localhost` or a home network. It looks the name up again at each delivery, and fails one that now leads somewhere private: "The receiver's address is not public."

The setting **`allow_private_addresses`** lets Marfa post there, including to `http://localhost:3000/marfa` on your own machine. The owner changes it after a recent sign-in, as [Settings](/run/settings) shows; a key can't.

The rules behind this guide are in the [events](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/events.md) chapter of the contract.
